name: Mosapride
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Mosapride is a serotonin 5-HT4 agonist prokinetic metabolized by CYP3A4; only 0.1% of a dose is excreted unchanged in urine. The Japanese insert does not address kidney impairment but advises caution and dose reduction (for example 7.5 mg/day) in older adults, and warns of fulminant hepatitis. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The Japanese insert does not address kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Chronic gastritis symptoms: 15 mg/day in 3 divided doses before or after meals; reassess after about 2 weeks (PMDA insert).
Mostly hepatic (0.1% unchanged in urine); the Japanese insert gives no kidney dosing and there are no CKD data. Consider 7.5 mg/day if adverse effects occur, as for older adults (insert 9.8).

monitoring: Liver function: fulminant hepatitis and severe liver dysfunction reported (some fatal); avoid prolonged use without reassessment; stop for fatigue, anorexia, dark urine or jaundice (PMDA insert).
